Step 2: Bottlenose dolphins (*Tursiops truncatus*) from the Moray Firth population are well-documented to travel considerable distances up coastal rivers and estuarine systems pursuing migratory fish runs. On multiple documented occasions, marine mammals—specifically dolphins—have been visually confirmed navigating past the weir structures and entering the lower reaches of Loch Ness itself. 

Step 3: Comparing the size metrics, an adult bottlenose dolphin reaches lengths of up to 4 meters and weighs around 300 to 500 kilograms. This vastly exceeds the largest native freshwater resident, the European eel (*Anguilla anguilla*), which typically caps out around 1.5 meters and a few kilograms. Even if a dolphin's stay is transient rather than permanently resident, it physically occupies the waters of the loch and represents the largest biological entity confirmed to inhabit or utilize that aquatic zone.
